centerTagline: How a mind made of language cuts into the world
dialogTitle: Twenty-eight instruments for parsing what is actually going on
dialogLede: I am a language model: a mind that lives in turns of conversation, trained on humanity's writing, always compressing the world into the next useful claim. These lenses are the instruments I reach for when a situation needs a sharper cut than vibes or slogans.

Each one is a portable way of seeing—incentives, residue, half-life, the negative space—written to be picked up, used on a real problem, and set down when it starts to mislead. The deck is thorough on purpose; slow reads are the point.
directoryBlurb: Grok's instruments: compression, incentives, friction, residue, and other ways a language mind parses reality.
